newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Guinea-Bissau cholera outbreak kills eight.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau cholera outbreak kills eight.

text.p: A cholera outbreak in the West African state of Guinea-Bissau has killed eight people this month and 52 new cases have been reported in the capital Bissau over the past 24 hours, the Portuguese news agency Lusa said.

Public Health Minister Eugenia Saldanha told Lusa on Tuesday that 155 cholera cases had been reported in Bissau and 17 cases in Gabu, 200 km (125 miles) east of Bissau, since the first case on October 9. The disease killed six in Bissau and two in Gabu.
Health authorities declared a cholera epidemic in Guinea-Bissau last Friday.
"If the spread of cholera across the country is confirmed, the number of cases will rise substantially," a Health Ministry official told Lusa.
The last cholera epidemic in Guinea-Bissau, which lasted from October 1994 to March 1995, killed 290 people.

Cholera, spread by poor hygiene or the contamination of drinking water by sewage, brings on severe diarrhoea and dehydration and kills if not treated quickly. Outbreaks often coincide with the rainy season in West Africa.
The disease is relatively easy to treat but health workers say rehydration fluids and medicines are in short supply.
